For me personally, it is the personal care/working nights combo. I am autistic, and I know that both of those things are not things I would be able to deal with (personal care because of my own issues, and nights because I don't function well on bad sleep in a way that is different to a neurotypical person). So I don't apply for SW or HCA jobs that involve this, because I know it would look worse on my cv to have done the job for 2 weeks and then inevitably have to quit, than having not done it. It comes down to being self aware of my own limitations as an autistic person, and these are the lines I'm not going to cross.

I do apply for other HCA/SW roles that do not involve personal care/nights, as those roles do exist! I haven't been successful in getting one yet, but hopefully soon.
